intended: always all o, k: Owner, c: Cleanup | (dispose[o] and k.parent = o and k not in Disposed and c in Registered - Ran and c.on = o) implies ((not runNow[c]) until dispose[k])
why: The claim only orders a parent's sub-owner disposal against the parent's own cleanups, but the formula's second conjunct instead constrains the relative dispose order between two sibling sub-owners (newest-created-first), something the claim's name never mentions and that has nothing to do with cleanups. Take an owner o with two children j (older) and k (younger) and no cleanups registered on o at all: the claim 'an owner disposes its sub owners before its own cleanups' is trivially satisfied (there are no cleanups to order), yet the full formula is still violated if j happens to be disposed before k, a scenario the claim itself has nothing to say about.
